conversations._note: The game's opening words, shown over a dark screen (src/ui/intro.ts), one line to a page.

lines.text: Forty autumns I've kept the walls of Kettle Notch. Folk call it a hobby. Silas calls it a waste of good cider weather.
It's a good town. Maples, cider, a fair every harvest, and not one soul in it wondering why anyone would build a farm wall halfway up a mountain.
There were a great many of us, once. Now there's me, and I've a bad knee.
Still, it's mostly lifting. Lift the stone, mumble over it, mind your back, and the winter stays up the mountain where it belongs.
...Hm. That's frost on the glass. In September.
Eldwin kneels at the wall and lays a hand on a stone. A faint rune glows, then gutters out.
Hm. You're not meant to be on this side, little ones.
Up you come. Back where you belong.
The wardstone's runes stutter. A crack runs through it, and cold mist spills from the gap.
So this is where you've been bleeding, old friend.
That's done me in for the week.

conversations._note: The first time the cold that stays sets in after a win (decision 0405), before its card (src/ui/results.ts). Matt chose the line.

lines.text: My knee'll tell me about that one tonight.
